chimney / dormer brick stack on roof
stone wall front face with door and windows

answer.evidence: The silhouette widens from 4 px at row 20 to 79 px at row 50 and stays wide. This is a sloped tiled roof plane covering rows 20-63. It ends in a dark eave line and shadow at rows 64-65 (L=15 across the columns scanned). Below it is a stone front wall of about 30 rows (66-95) with a door and two windows. The roof is the top surface and the wall is the front face, so this is a 3/4 view. The brick stack on the roof is part of the roof plane and is drawn on the same slope.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a ruined house with a tiled roof, stone walls, a broken door and overgrowth. It sits at 27 visible tones per tile against 12 and 10 for the references, and its near-flat coverage is 0% like theirs. Only 10% of its dark edge pixels are near-neutral (references 7% and 9%), so its outlines carry a tint and read as dark material tones, not a black sticker line. The roof has per-tile highlights and scallops with about 5 lightness steps, close to the references. Moss, vines, holes and debris add grain and variation. The stone wall is shaded stone by stone and shows no large flat areas. It looks a little busier and more broken than the clean references, which fits a ruin, and a careful artist would accept it next to them.
